acceptance_criteria: Spoofing test (same name, wrong SPKI) returns NoTrustedPath. All 4 tests pass.
description:
Implement private fn find_trust_anchor(chain, anchors, verifier_context) -> Result<usize>
that locates the trust anchor terminating the chain.

## What

Walk anchors[]. For each anchor, check:
1. anchor.subject DN == chain.last().tbs_certificate.issuer, using names_match() from PKIX-drv.
2. anchor.subject_public_key_info bytes == chain.last().tbs_certificate.authority_key_identifier's
   key identifier hash (or direct SPKI comparison after PKIX-o76 lands).

Return Ok(anchor_index) for the FIRST matching anchor, Err(Error::NoTrustedPath) if none match.

## Security requirement
Name-only matching MUST NOT be used. A self-signed leaf whose subject == anchor.subject
but with a different key must be rejected. SPKI comparison is the defense.
After PKIX-o76 TrustAnchor holds (subject_name, spki) directly — compare both.

## Tests (externally-generated DER hex literals)
- Single anchor, matching name + SPKI -> Ok(0)
- Two anchors, second one matches -> Ok(1)
- Anchor with matching name but different SPKI -> Err(NoTrustedPath)   [security test]
- Anchor with mismatched name -> Err(NoTrustedPath)
- Zero anchors -> delegates to check_inputs; guard here is belt-and-suspenders

## Depends on
PKIX-drv (names_match), PKIX-1tb (trust anchor matching primitives), PKIX-o76 (TrustAnchor shape)
title: pkix-path: find_trust_anchor — subject DN + SPKI matching
